title: Diabetes, hypertension and CKD together
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, kidney disease and any related hypertension and dialysis status.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for chronic kidney disease and type 2 diabetes.

HPI
The patient is an 80-year-old male who presents today for a routine follow-up of his chronic kidney disease and type 2 diabetes. He reports feeling generally stable at this time. He notes that he continues to manage his blood glucose levels primarily through dietary modifications. He denies any recent acute changes in his renal function or new symptoms of systemic illness. He is currently maintaining his nutrition and expresses no concerns regarding his current management plan.

Medication List
1. Multivitamin
2. Vitamin D supplement

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 132/78 mmHg
Heart Rate: 72 bpm
Temperature: 98.6 F
Weight: 185 lbs
SpO2: 97% on room air

Recent Labs
eGFR: 12 mL/min/1.73m2
HbA1c: 7.4%
Creatinine: 4.8 mg/dL

Review of Systems
The patient reports no chest pain, shortness of breath, or recent fevers. He denies any significant weight changes or changes in appetite. He denies any new-onset weakness or numbness in his extremities.

Social History
The patient lives at home with his wife. He enjoys gardening and watching television. He reports a sedentary lifestyle and denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Father had a history of cardiovascular disease. Mother had a history of type 2 diabetes.

Exam
The patient is an alert and oriented 80-year-old male in no acute distress. Skin is dry but intact. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Heart sounds are regular with no murmurs. Abdomen is soft, non-tender, and non-distended. Extremities are symmetric with no edema noted.

Assessment
1. End stage renal disease: The patient's laboratory values confirm an eGFR of 12, consistent with his diagnosis of end stage renal disease.
2. Type 2 diabetes: The patient's HbA1c remains stable while managed solely through his current dietary regimen.

Plan
1. Continue current dietary management for type 2 diabetes.
2. Monitor renal function and electrolytes with follow-up labs in three months.
3. Follow up in the clinic in 90 days.

Electronically signed, H. Tanaka, MD, 05/14/2026
explanations: Type 2 diabetes and CKD are linked by the 'with' convention unless the provider says otherwise: E11.22 (HCC 37).
The CKD stage is coded in addition: N18.6.

distractors.why: The 'with' convention presumes the diabetes caused the CKD.
E11.22 says to use an additional code for the CKD stage.
